text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3.4% today as oil prices surged on geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran's escalation of attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint for global oil supplies—drove U.S. crude up sharply on Friday, pushing prices toward $102 a barrel. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly flow to the bottom line, and the stock has climbed 15.6% over two weeks as this regional risk premium has built in.

The move also reflects a widening gap between the headline oil price and what traders call the "real" cost to physically deliver crude: tanker rates have surged so much that oil costs roughly $38 more per barrel to ship than the spot price suggests. That tightness in physical supply—combined with uncertainty over U.S. policy toward Iran—has kept energy markets on edge and rewarded producers holding inventory in the ground.
